title: Weapons
rulesText:
As a member of a premier PMC with leading military R&D, characters get access to a wide range of weapons to use against their many foes. Weapons in Calamari are divided across weapon classes, each weapon class has a universal statistic associated with it allowing players to select whatever weapon of their choosing that fits into that weapon class and simply copy the stats. Within those classes are weapon families that can alter the specific stats or functions of a weapon. Family costs are added onto the base weapon's costs when purchased.

Ammo is handled in turns of ammunition- where the total reserve ammo is how many turns of ammo you have for that weapon in total, and the turns per magazine are the amount of turns you can fire until empty. When firing, mark down a turn of ammunition spent from your magazine and your total reserves, and keep track of how many you have left in the magazine.

Reloading allows you to restock the turns of ammo in your magazine. When you reload, reset the turns of ammo in your weapon's magazine to its capacity. Reloading from empty applies a -1 to all actions that turn, while reloading with ammo left in the magazine will apply a -1 malus to your shooting test.

Weapon stats are formatted where PEN is a weapon's penetration value, DMG is the base damage a weapon will do to targets before modifiers and MOS, RSV is the total turns of ammo a weapon has, and CAP is how many turns are in a magazine.

The true middle ground when it comes to weapons, they dominate mid-range engagements but take a hit in CQB. These weapons come with the ability to Burst Fire, enabling them to fire a tight burst towards a single opponent for more damage, at the expense of less dice.

Gain a +1 bonus when in Close range of the target.
You can Overclock your rifle to gain a +1 to penetration and +2 to damage for one turn during an encounter. After an overclock, results below 5 will automatically jam for the next two turns.

description: Shotguns are the kings of close quarters, chambered in a variety of 12 gauge shells, and occasionally in 8 gauge, they will annihilate anything foolish enough to stand less than 10 meters in front of them. This high damage potential does come with the caveat of a massive damage drop-off over long distances. These weapons can also be used as makeshift breaching devices and have destructive abilities against soft walls.

Chambered from anything between 7.62x51 AP, 338 Lapua, and .300 Norma these weapons are perfect for dropping individual targets long before they know what hit them, made all the better with their armour-penetrating rounds that can hit targets behind soft walls and cover. The major downside however is drawbacks for trying to use them in CQC and their low ammo count. Make each shot count.

Despite this mix of calibers, their main purpose isn't to inflict pinpoint precision damage but to instead shatter the will and the cover of anyone in front of their field of fire. title: Grenades
rulesText:
Handy little tools in a pinch, throwables come in a variety of shapes and sizes with each one designed to carry out a specific task. These tasks range from stealth assassination, infantry removal, concealment, disorientation and anti-armour.

 When most grenades are thrown in combat, it prompts an opposed roll of the attacker's [Throw] against a defender's choice of action depending on the grenade. When out of combat, it requires an [Alertness] check to react in time, and then roll for their defensive action.

 Grenades can be thrown to medium range without issues, but at long range take a -1 malus and cannot be thrown further. 

 When rolling for acrobatics to evade, An MOS greater than 2 has the defender still standing, else- they are considered prone at the start of their next turn if they succeed. When bracing as a reaction, the character is considered bracing at the start of their next turn.

title: Repair Tool
description: Wrenches, Impact Drills, Blowtorches and more. Repair tools let Technical Engineers fix up drones and vehicles, or more creatively seal off doors and destroy enemy infrastructure.
rulesText:
[Repair]
Vehicle equivalent of an AFAK, uses a tinker roll to fix vehicle critical damage and minor damage. Can be used to damage or sabotage enemy vehicles or infrastructure. Unlimited uses. Can also do the opposite. When repairing, make a Tinker test to determine the amount of damage repaired. Prioritizes Critical Damage first, and then fixes minor damage. Vehicle crews 'relax' when their vehicles are being repaired. For parts with HP and drones, multiply the result by 2 for how much damage is repaired.

rulesText:

rulesText:

Can throw med-packs to teammates with a threshold of 3 + the amount of range bands between you and the target starting at +0 for close range, to a maximum of +2 long range

 Only purchaseable through the Bastogne Martel Foundation.

rulesText: Raider is an expert at getting into anywhere, loud or quiet and being the tip of the spear with SMGs, Shotguns, breaching charges, and Ninebangs. The Raider is a stealthy class, but also the most useful in room clearing when things go loud.

rulesText:

Tinker test against specific thresholds.
Open all doors immediately. Has a threshold of 2 for normal doors, 3 for heavy doors, and then 4 for reinforced doors. Can also be used to cut through fences and other thinner materials quickly.
Makes no noise. Provides a bright light that can attract attention.

3 hex AOE

Upon defender MOF of 2, they are [Stunned] and lose their turn. If used before combat starts, will cause friendlies to have initiative first instead of enemies.

description: The initial model was made in a cave with scraps and with CMF shielding- sometimes just recharged the devices that it hit. But- now with a touch from Gold Coast- it consistently disables everything around it.
rulesText:
[EMP][Deploy]
AOE: C
Disables all non-friendly electronics and lights around the user.
If indoors with no natural lighting, it applies a pitch black effect to the room and any adjacent. If there is natural lighting, it will apply ‘very dimly lit’ to the room. At night, can be used to make anywhere pitch black.

Requires 2 turns of rapid movement (sprinting or more) or 4 turns of normal movement to recharge. Can also use a bonus action to wiggle in place to charge for a normal movement turn.

title: STALKER Digital Presence Reducer

+1 dice to stealth rolls while in use. Invisible to all cameras and drones while active. Unpingable while active. Actions no longer cause noise and won't cause notice checks when not in line of sight.
Lasts 3 turns.
Requires 2 turns of rapid movement (sprinting or more) or 4 turns of normal movement to recharge. Can also use a bonus action to wiggle in place to charge for a normal movement turn.

All attacking or notice rolls have to flip a coin. Upon tails, they can attack or try to notice. When enemies know that you have camouflage, they no longer have to roll notice to attack.

When active, provides an extra dice to stealth and disguise rolls.
Lasts 2 turns, breaks at the end of the second turn.
Requires 2 turns of rapid movement (sprinting or more) or 4 turns of normal movement to recharge. Can also use a bonus action to wiggle in place to charge for a normal movement turn.

Will cause characters within the room it's fired in or one hex from the round path to make a defensive suppression test against a threshold of 4. Requires a [Deploy] action to set up, if not set up- the shooting test takes a -1 malus.

title: Technical Engineer
rulesText: Standoff munitions is the name, drones are the game. Technical Engineers are experts in both vehicular warfare and using drones to attack, distract, or blow up targets. Technicical Engineers are experts in tinkering and tech, and can utilize drones such as the XMQ-88 ‘Demo Dog’ and XMQ-16 ‘Fire Hornet’ proficiently.
description: The drones... They speak to me.

title: XMQ-16 Fire Hornet
description: Taking the concept of the RQ-16 T-HAWK and MQ-8 Fire Scout, the Fire Hornet combines the concepts into a smaller, quadcopter platform. Equipped with a gun gimbal and BUDDI Spotting software, the Fire Scout offers engineers the flexibility to fight from multiple angles, or flank targets they can't get to from the sky.
rulesText:
[Airborne][Repairable][Deploy][Datalink]
General: 1 | All Weapons: 2 | Endurance: 1 | Notice: 2 | Investigation: 1
Range Modifiers: +1 C, -1 L, -2 ELR
Ammo: 6
10 HP | AC:0
PEN: 1 | Damage: 4

title: XMQ-88 Demolition Dog
description: Developed to solve an ethics concern of K-9 units, and subsequently creating new ones with unmanned drones, the XMQ-88 Demo-Dog is an unmanned, autonomous, quadrupedal robot. It can be equipped with a variety of equipment, from suppressed SMGs for a frontline role, marksman rifles as a remote sniper sentry, to even LMGs for suppressive fire. It even makes noises when you pet it!
rulesText:
[Ground][Repairable][Deploy][Datalink]
General: 1 | All Weapons: 2 | Endurance: 2 | Notice: 1 | Stealth: 1 
 30 HP | AC:1

title: XMQ-88 Demo-Dog [Frontline]
description: The original, and ever beloved Demo Dog armed with a GCR-500 Assault Rifle. Don't fix what ain't broken.
rulesText:
[Ground][Repairable][Deploy][Datalink]
General: 1 | All Weapons: 2 | Endurance: 2 | Notice: 1 | Stealth: 1
Range Modifiers: +1 M , -1 L , -1 ELR
Ammo: 6
30 HP | AC:1
PEN: 2 | Damage: 5

title: XMQ-88 Demo-Dog [Stealth]
description: Customised stealth package for the demo-dog. Originally created for Special Reconnaissance teams and SOCOM requirements, the package installs whisper quiet servos, strips unnecessary armour, and swaps the standard belt fed GCR-500 for a suppressed .300 blackout variant called the ‘Kitty Kat’.
rulesText:
[Ground][Repairable][Deploy][Datalink]
General: 1 | All Weapons: 2 | Endurance: 2 | Notice: 1 | Stealth: 1 [+2]
Range Modifiers: +1 C, -1 L, -2 ELR
Ammo: 6
30 HP | AC:0
PEN: 1 | Damage: 4

title: XMQ-88 Demo-Dog [Marksman]
description: Dedicated marksman variant for Long Range Recon and endurance. Strips down the armor much like the stealth variant in favor of an advanced sensor suite.
rulesText:
[Ground][Repairable][Deploy][Datalink]
General: 1 | All Weapons: 2 | Endurance: 2 | Notice: 2 | Stealth: 1
Range Modifiers: -1 C | +1 L | -1 ELR
Ammo: 6
30 HP | AC:0
PEN: 2 | Damage: 6

title: XMQ-88 Demo-Dog [Gunner]
description: Based on prototypes found in 2018, the Gunner variant offers more firepower and ammo in exchange for poor close range performance due to the weight of the machine gun.
rulesText:
[Ground][Repairable][Deploy][Datalink]
General: 1 | All Weapons: 2 | Endurance: 2 | Notice: 1 [+2] | Stealth: 1
Range Modifiers: -1 C | +1 M | -1 L | -1 ELR
Ammo: 6
30 HP | AC:0
PEN: 2 | Damage: 5

title: XMQ-17 UCAV 'Magic Missile'
description: The whir of electric motors and the buzz of small drones have become the new age stuka siren. Equipped with an anti-infantry warhead
rulesText:
[Airborne][Explosive][Deploy][Datalink]
PEN 1 | DMG 7
AOE 2
When deployed, the user's turn ends immediately. When attacking an enemy, the defender rolls acrobatics if they wish to dodge, their armor with cover bonuses if they wish to brace, or their respective weapons with a -1 dice malus if they want to shoot it out of the sky. Uses a Drive check when deployed. Fumbles pre-detonate the warhead.

title: XMQ-18 UCAV-AT 'Bigger Magic Missile'
description: The whir of electric motors and the buzz of small drones have become the new age stuka siren. Equipped with a shaped charge warhead for vehicles.
rulesText:
[Airborne][Explosive][Deploy][Datalink]
PEN 3 | DMG 8
AOE 0
When deployed, the user's turn ends immediately. When attacking an enemy, the defender rolls acrobatics if they wish to dodge, their armor with cover bonuses if they wish to brace, or their respective weapons with a -1 dice malus if they want to shoot it out of the sky. Uses a Drive check when deployed. Fumbles pre-detonate the warhead.

title: Fire Support
rulesText: Experts in putting lead downrange and mortar arcs, Fire Support focuses on suppression and indirect fire. Supports get exclusive access to LMGs, Automatic Shotguns and the X-90 remote mortar system but know that Fire Supports require setup before they can fire.
description: Statistically, on average, I shoot all of you about nine times- no twenty-er... Enough to make swiss soldiers.

title: X-89 AMS (Auto-Mortar)
description: Simplifies the math of indirect fire into a 'point and click' adventure game. Allows the user to set up a remote mortar, designate targets, and then deliver ordnance from anywhere within an AO accurately.
rulesText:
[H-Wep][Deploy][Datalink]
Requires a line of sight to the sky, along with minimal obstruction. Requires a deploy action to place, uses H-wep as the attacker test. Cannot hit targets inside of buildings or with strong overhead cover.

Before a mission, choose an amount of rounds, up to the maximum capacity, from each type that has been purchased.
Ammo: 4

title: X-89 HE rounds
description: Standard High Explosive Ordnance. Kaboom.
rulesText:
[Explosive]
H-wep attacker test vs Acrobatics defender test.
Pen 1 | 8 DMG
2 hex AOE

title: X-89 ACERM rounds (Guided)
description: Guided penetration rounds that change trajectory mid air to strike a target accurately.
rulesText:
[Explosive][Datalink]
H-wep attacker test vs Acrobatics defender test.
Pen 3 | 8 DMG
1 hex AOE
If the target is pinged, the attacker test is made with an extra dice. If a vehicle is designated, the attack is guaranteed to hit unless countermeasures are used.

title: X-89 SMK rounds (Smoke)
description: Creates a plume of smoke around a designated location to cut off lines of sight.
rulesText:
[Obscure]
H-wep Attacker test against a threshold of 3
Pen 1 | No DMG
AOE 3
Applies ‘very dimly lit’ effect to an area. Removes [Pinged] if a target is no longer visible with smoke.

title: X-89 SRN rounds (Sauron)
description: Hangs in the sky via a parachute and pings targets with a bright red glare. Can be shot down.
rulesText:
[Ping][Loitering]
H-Weapons attacker test vs lower Disguise or Stealth defender test.
No DMG | AOE: LR
Pings all enemies within Long Range of where it hovers over
Loiters for 2 turns.
Upon fumble, the Sauron will tag no targets. Can be shot down.

title: X-89 EMP rounds
description: Starshell rounds’ bigger brother. No longer are you just jamming comms, but now you're full on cutting all power to devices in an area.
rulesText:
[EMP]
H-wep Attacker test against a threshold of 3
No DMG | AOE: C
Disables all non-friendly electronics and lights around the user.
If indoors with no natural lighting, it applies a pitch black effect to the room and any adjacent. If there is natural lighting, it will apply ‘very dimly lit’ to the room. At night, it can be used to make anywhere pitch black.
Electronics will return in 1 turn from when it was deployed.

title: X-89 ILM rounds (Illumination)
description: Hangs in the sky and illuminates a wide area, also rings the dinnerbell to where the fight is.
rulesText:
[Vision]
H-wep Attacker test against a threshold of 3
No DMG
Removes all lighting and weather conditions in the area.
Blinds Thermal and Night vision.

title: Resupply Bag
description: A bag of spare ammo. Includes auto-feeders to rapidly refill magazines with them.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Resupply]
Resupplies all ammo and grenades, requires someone to come directly to the hex it is deployed on to resupply. Each party member can only resupply once. Can throw supply packs to teammates with a threshold of 3 + the amount of range bands between you and the target starting at +0 for close range, to a maximum of +2 long range

title: Spitfire Feeder System
description: Utilizing a backpack feeder and a gyroscopic camera mount, the spitfire allows you to put down an unmatched amount of firepower at the expense of melting barrels and making the logistics officer incredibly angry at you.
rulesText:
[Suppression]
The stabilizer removes the ability to mount in exchange for removing penalties for moving and shooting. Allows the user to supress a second set of six hexes. Barrels melt at three turns of consequtive supression. reloading in the same turn has no penalty as ammo is fed from pack.

title: Juggernaut Suit
description: Repurposed EOD suit equipped with a half-exo to assist with movement. Provides a two stage armor system, where the outer layer of armor ‘soaks’ damage before it begins to strip and fall apart with further impacts.
rulesText:
[Armor][Half-Exo]
The suit soaks up to 150 HP of damage, and all Armor tests while in the suit are made at AC0. If the attacker wins the test, damage is dealt to the pool normally (MoS x weapon damage). If the attacker fails the test, the shot is still absorbed, and the armor soaks the weapon's base damage (MoS of 1) from the pool. At 0 HP the armor is shredded. The user now takes damage against their wound and instant death thresholds and has AC0.

Exosuit limbs are now part of the armor. Each body part (Legs, Arms, Torso) has 1/5 of the suit's current HP at the moment it is shot, and an attack to a limb cannot inflict more damage to the suit than what a limb has. When a limb's armor is destroyed, further damage to that area is tested against their wound and instant death thresholds. A destroyed leg inflicts [Cripple], and two destroyed legs inflict [Debilitated]. Arms and torso have no extra effect. [Deploy] dons or removes the suit. If the suit is [Disabled], the user is [Debilitated]. A [Repair] action will always repair the total suit HP.

title: MP-APS
description: A portable version of the Active Protection System, the MPAPS is a hard kill countermeasure for defeating most munitions such as 40mms, grenades, rockets, and even drones. When deployed, it shines a bright green light on areas it is protecting when active, and flashes red when inactive.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Intercept]
3 charges.
20HP, benefits from cover bonuses. Destroys all munitions from UCAVs, 40mms, Rockets, and grenades in close range of it. When a munition is destroyed, it will detonate at the edge of the AOE. It won't destroy friendly munitions. Each charge protects an area for a turn when it’s active.

title: Ammo Bags
description: A bag of unique ammo types, includes auto-feeders to rapidly fill a magazine with them.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Resupply]
5 charges
Before a mission, choose an amount of charges, up to the capacity, from each ammo type that is purchased. When deployed and interacted with, gain two turns of a specific ammo type for your primary or secondary. Can throw ammo packs to teammates with a threshold of 3 + the amount of range bands between you and the target starting at +0 for close range, to a maximum of +2 long range.

title: Stopping Power
description: Loads the rounds with some extra spice, or well... Grain. It's basically overpressure and high grain ammunition.
rulesText: Increases the weapon’s damage by 2.

title: Subsonics
description: Underloads and optimizes the rounds to sit at just below supersonic and transonic speeds. Removes the distinct 'crack' of supersonic rounds and makes your shot signature significantly quieter as a result. Doesn't mean it won't ‘whizz’ and ‘hiss’ though.
rulesText: When in stealth, wont cause an alertness check when firing. When disengaged, firing will not re-engage you. When cloaked, it will keep you cloaked even when firing. Reduces weapon damage by 1.

title: High Velocity
description: Optimizes the rounds to shoot faster and flatter. It won't make them any quieter, but some people say it turns it into a point and shoot adventure game.
rulesText: Increases Long, ELR, and EELR Range Band modifier with a +1 bonus.

title: Match Grade
description: High quality ammunition built for competition shooting. Improves close range performance through improved powders that fit better within the tolerances of the firearm. Essentially, bougie ammo.
rulesText: Increases Close and Medium Range Band modifier with a +1 bonus.

title: Medic
rulesText: Medics are the backbone of any good fire team and are the only class focused on keeping others in the fight and buffing them as much as they can. Medics get access to the surgical kit and specialized stims to heal wounds, increase focus, or generally provide buffs in a pinch.
description: With one hand I save life, with the other hand I take it, Actually it's the same hand, but that don't sound as good.

title: Nanite Pouch
description: Contains all the stimulants and boosters a medic can carry, from regenerative nanites that heal you, to performance enhancing ones that let you react faster. Includes a stim pistol for ranged applications.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Medical]
Holds all of the nanite stims for a medic. Before a mission, choose an amount of injectors, up to an overall total of the capacity, from each nanite type that is purchased. Comes with a stim pistol which requires an [L-Wep] test against a threshold of 3 + the amount of range bands between you and the target, starting at +0 for close range, to a maximum of +2 long range. Cannot fire past Long Range.

title: Regen Nanite Kit (RNK)
description: Advanced nanomachines automatically help stop bleeding, apply painkillers, and make getting shot a little less un-fun.
rulesText:
[Stimulant]
Heal a flesh wound every turn, if no flesh wounds heal a deep wound every 2 turns.
Lasts for (1d6 turns+ Medical Skill)/2 turns rounded up.

title: Shock Nanite Kit (SNK)
description: A concoction of nanites from every kind to stave off death and keep someone in the fight. Painkillers, coagulants, and stimulants get someone back on their feet instantly.
rulesText:
[Stimulant]
Revives a character from DBNO instantly with only a flesh wound. The turn after- remove a flesh wound.

title: Traumadol Nanite Kit (TNK)
description: Retooled for killing any and all pain, Truamadol Nanites make the user feel nothing, other than emotion. We didn't disable that just yet.
rulesText:
[Stimulant]
Ignore the effects of wound modifiers on tests, or any afflictions caused by wounds or damage to yourself. A character can still enter system shock.
Lasts for (1d6 turns+ Medical Skill)/2 turns rounded up.

title: Adrenal Nanite Kit (DTNK)
description: Created to simulate a release of adrenaline via nanites, the Adrenal Nanites give you a kick of energy in the moment.
rulesText:
[Booster]
Adds another standard action.
Lasts for the turn

title: Nootropic Nanite Kit (HANK)
description: Utilizing the power of nootropics and nicknamed 'high alert', these nanites give you a much more powerful boost of energy as they also mix in adrenaline. Leading to a single use but highly effective combat stimulant.
rulesText:
[Booster]
Adds another standard and movement action, reduces maluses from movement by 1.
Lasts for the turn.

title: Ligament Restorative Kit (LRK)
rulesText:
[Booster]
Temporary increases all Alertness/Body skills to level 2. Any skills above level 2 remain at their level.
Lasts for two turns.

title: Metabolic Overdrive Kit (MOK)
rulesText:
[Booster]
Temporary increases all Alertness/Body skills to level 3. Any skills above level 3 remain at their level.
Lasts for two turns. Causes the character to become [Exhausted] on the turn after the effect ends reducing their Alertness and Body skills to 1 for that turn.

title: Deployable Barricade
description: An enlarged version of the deployable cover, this version unfolds rapidly after a few seconds when a cord on its base is yanked, flooding the kevlar with a rapidly expanding foam that unfolds it and then hardens into a HESCO-like barricade.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Obscure]
3 Charges
Creates a 4 hex long piece of tall cover in any direction next to the user. This cover cannot be picked up and re-deployed like the Deployable Cover. Each hex must be on the same elevation, or it cannot be placed. The package can be thrown to a maximum of close range.

title: C/HUD Lifesaver
description: A small quadcopter fitted with a microdrone dispenser. Each microdrone is loaded with stimulants to heal someone during a fight that lands and inject small dosages of nanites on the target whenever they take damage. Also has an ascii face on its underside.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Airborne][Stimulant]
Uptime: 2 turns | Downtime: 2 turn
When deployed, designate an infantry target. This target heals one deep wound every turn it is active, or two flesh wounds if there aren't any deep wounds. Upon the target being given enough damage to cause instant death, will instead only take 2 deep wounds. If the target enters system shock or otherwise enters DBNO- they are instantly revived with only a flesh wound, but still contribute to the total amount of downs they have taken.

These effects only last during the drone’s uptime, and upon that uptime running out- the drone will return to the medic who deployed it. While deployed, the drone can be given a new target to heal via a [Deploy] action.

title: C/HUD Flowstate
description: A small quadcopter fitted with a microdrone dispenser. Each microdrone is loaded with painkillers to ensure someone doesn't feel the pain during a fight. Due to the powerful nature of the painkillers- less microdrones are needed per dosage, and it has a longer uptime at the cost of less healing.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Airborne][Booster]
Uptime: 2 turns | Downtime: 1 turns
When deployed, designate an infantry target. This target heals one flesh wound every turn it is active, or a deep wound every 2 turns if there aren't any flesh wounds. While with the designated target, the target ignores the effects of wound modifiers on tests, or any afflictions caused by wounds or damage to them. They can still enter system shock.

These effects only last during the drone’s uptime, and upon that uptime running out- the drone will return to the medic who deployed it. While deployed, the drone can be given a new target to heal via a [Deploy] action on the medic’s turn.

title: Sharpshooter
rulesText: Expert marksman, the Sharpshooter Class focuses on eliminating targets of opportunity or high-threat enemies with DMRs and Sniper Rifles. Sharpshooters get exclusive access to sniper rifles and equipment such as BUDDI HUD integrations, SOFLAMs, and EXACTO rounds for extreme distances.
description: Boom. Headshot. [Trumpets begin playing]

title: Hummingbird Reconnaissance Drone
description: Built off the chassis of the PD-105 Black Hornet, Hummingbird reconnaissance drones are a unique modification tying in BUDDI spotting software, Infrared imaging, and a hardened datalink uplink.
rulesText:
[Airborne][Repairable][Deploy][Ping][Datalink][IR]
User carried
Uptime: 1 | Downtime: 1
1 general | 3 notice | 2 stealth | 2 investigation
Spot traps, gadgets, vehicles, and more within the world hex via a quick scan before returning to the user. Causes a stealth or disguise test, using the lower, against any contact in the area. Uses Thermal/IR imaging.

title: Silver Bird UAV (SUAV)
description: Built off of the Marine's SUAV, the Silver Bird is an autonomous drone that orbits the user at a high altitude to mark targets. Has only NV. Pings for every turn it is up.
rulesText:
[Airborne][Repairable][Deploy][Ping][Designate][Datalink][NVG]
User Carried
Uptime: 3 turns | Downtime: 2 turns
1 general | 2 notice | 2 acrobatics | 2 investigation
Pings in a large area, extending to 3 world hexes from and including the encounter area. Causes a stealth or disguise test, using the lower, against any contact in the area. Will not spot gadgets, traps, drones, or anyone indoors. Has a LAM and can [Designate] targets. Cannot be used indoors.

title: Bumblebee Echolocator MAV
description: Survey drone utilizing echolocation to mark moving enemies. Shakes the ground when activated, but will always provide a ping. Can be shot down easily once noticed, and is kinda fat.
rulesText:
[Airborne][Repairable][Deploy][Mark][Datalink]
Pre-Deployed
2 charges
When activated using a [Deploy] action, it creates a large humming noise as it echolocates targets on the ground. It will scan everything within the world hex and one hex around, and [Mark] all targets.

title: Grappling Hook
rulesText:
[Deploy][Traversal]
2 Charges.
When deployed using a [Deploy] action against an incline or vertical surface, it allows you to quickly climb up it using a Climb test with a threshold of your armor class. The grappling hook can be deployed up to three stories (6 steps in elevation) and only within close range of a ledge using a Throw test against the steps of elevation of the ledge you’re grappling to. A grappling hook can be re-used if picked up after deployment. In Grand Operations It can be used to override the original climb test with the one it provides.

title: Zipline
rulesText:
[Deploy][Traversal][M-wep]
3 Charges
When deployed using a [Deploy] action, pick a hex further than medium range and within line of sight, abiding by elevation rules. When a hex is selected that isn't the one the shooter is on- they can fire the Zipline using an M-Wep test against a threshold of 1+ the amount of range bands between them and the selected hex (LR would be 2 EELR being 4). Upon failure- the zipline fails to catch and the charge is spent. Characters who interact with the zipline can sacrifice one range band of movement for moving between both points of the zipline freely. In Grand Operations- it allows you to traverse up to 6 hexes unimpeded.

title: Special Ammo
description: Special ammo allows for sharpshooters to have a greater effect with their bullets than just killing people. From disabling electronics with a condensed EMP round, to punching through even the heaviest of body armor with AP rounds.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Shoot]
4 rounds
Before a mission, choose an amount of rounds, up to the capacity, from each ammo type that is purchased. Using a [Deploy] action, you can replace the current turn of ammo loaded with that round, and then fire with its effects. Can only be used with Marksman and Sniper Rifles.

title: LRE (Lure) Round
description: Lures an enemy towards a specific location. Has a lower drop, and a lower lethality, and makes a cute chirping sound.
rulesText: Reduces damage by 3, but makes a ping and a noise that makes enemies investigate within medium range of its impact point. Subsonic.

title: AP Round
description: High penetration bullets that improve the penetration value of a weapon by 1.
rulesText: Increases round penetration by 1. Negates the effects of two stage armor systems (juggernaut suits)

title: SMRT (Smart) Round
description: Locks onto a target and adjusts for bullet drop and windage automatically. Effectively removes the math from shooting, beyond gauging travel time.
rulesText: Can only be used on marked or pinged targets, Adds a flat +1 to the roll.

title: EMP Round
description: Creates a small electromagnetic pulse around the impact point.
rulesText: Disables and disrupts electronics for 1 turn with a 1 hex AOE where it landed. Can disrupt APS and vehicle systems if aimed correctly.

title: Trapper
rulesText: Unlike their close Sharpshooter cousins, Trappers focus on ambushes with traps and some ingenuity along with sabotage and stealth. Trappers also get access to the Cyberwarfare Suite, but also access Claymores, anti-tank mines and more.
description: A gift for you, no charge... oh wait, explosive charge!

title: Shock Sticks
description: Shock Sticks are quiet, non-lethal traps which can be used to stealthily dispatch guards or patrols, bar the noise of them being tased.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Throw][Electric]
Attacker Throw vs Defender Acrobatics [Throw]
or
Attacker Disguise vs Defender Alertness [Trap]
3 Sticks
3 hex AOE
Loiters for 2 turns when activated

Forces a Body check against 4 when caught in the trap.
-Upon failure, you are tased, forced prone, and take a flesh wound.
-Upon success, you can disable the shock stick with a standard action- or leave its AOE.

title: Claymores
description: Shotgun in a tin. Riddles a target with ball bearings when triggered, and will auto-detonate by itself whenever something passes by. Don't worry, it won't fire if friendlies are near.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Explosive]
Attacker Disguise vs Defender Alertness
3 Claymores
8 DMG | PEN 2
4 hex diagonal AOE
If a contact or object enters between the diagonal AOE of the claymore- it will trigger.

title: Lil Mac'
description: KNOCKOUT! When activated, Lil Mac springs up from the ground and smacks into the enemy’s face, knocking them down.
rulesText:
[Deploy]
Attacker Disguise vs Defender Alertness
2x Lil Mac’s
When triggered, mine props up and knocks the defender out for a total of 4 turns. Silent. Can be re-used if picked up.

title: C4
description: Better known as 'jeep stuff', C4 is a malleable material that when introduced to an electric charge—detonates spectacularly. There are a lot of use cases. Get creative.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Throw][Explosive]
Attacker Throw vs Defender Acrobatics [Throw]
or
Attacker Disguise vs Defender Alertness [Trap]
3 charges
4 hex AOE
10 DMG | PEN 3

title: M5 SLAM
description: Jeep stuff's younger, more tech-savvy cousin, M5 SLAMs are AT/Demo charges that can be set to detonate under a variety of circumstances. Easy to program, easy to detonate, and even float in water to act as aquatic mines.
rulesText:
[Deploy][Throw][Explosive]
Attacker Throw vs Defender Acrobatics [Throw]
or
Attacker Disguise vs Defender Alertness [Trap]

Can be deployed on any surface with either:
- Timed detonation (turn count)
- Attack detonation (trap)
- Remote detonation (manual)

15 DMG | PEN 3

title: Cyberwarfare Suite
description: It’s a ThinkPad. You’re not leaving this job for a while brother, and this thing isn’t breaking unless you shoot it with a tank.
rulesText:
[Datalink][Deploy]
Provides access to the cyberwarfare suite. All hacks are successful and the opposed tests are made to determine how messy or clean an intrusion is. The attacker MOF is given to the defender as HEAT. The attacker always gives at least one HEAT to the defender. Certain hacks are more traceable than others, and take a traceability malus to the test as a byproduct.

HEAT is used to make actions against a team, and can either be spent to reduce their traceability malus by consuming an amount of HEAT, or for every 3 HEAT against a team, can be consumed to make a free hack against an enemy. This free hack will cause or be affected by MAP.

title: Cooldown
description: Automatically scrambles your position and traceable data to shake enemy cyberwarfare or intrusion countermeasure software.
rulesText: Lowers your HEAT by 2

title: Puppet
description: Manipulate basic device functions, such as opening/closing doors and deactivating/accessing cameras.
rulesText: Allows you to open select doors and see through cameras. Does not work with drones, combat vehicles, or HUDs.

title: Ping
description: Accesses local cameras and devices and pings contacts it can find.
rulesText: [-1 Traceability] Pings all enemies within 16 hexes. If someone’s electronics are [Disabled]- they are not pinged.

title: Sever
description: Accesses a specific target and cuts their connection to all downlink and uplink connections, effectively 'severing' them from their own command.
rulesText: [-1 Traceability] Disable an enemy's ability to call reinforcements, mark targets, or control drones for 2 Turns.

title: Feedback
description: Deafens a target and scrambles their communications system, making them unable to communicate with others through a deafening tone. Very effective in annoying enemies to forcefully disable their radios, or disrupting them entirely
rulesText: [-2 Traceability] Interrupts an enemy and applies a -1 to all actions for their turn. Countered by disabling [Datalink] via a bonus action.

title: Traceback
description: Ping's bigger brother, penetrates into an enemy datalink to trace it back to everything using it. Pings any and every enemy on the local network.
rulesText: [-3 Traceability] Pings all enemies within the world hex.

title: Mass Hack
description: Brute forcing one's way into all local networks, this locks out all enemy users from the datalink. However, it will also spread to the rest of the connected signals, leading to a mass lockout that spreads to vehicles, drones, and more.
rulesText: [-4 traceability] [Disables] all enemy electronics within the world hex. Disables radio, cameras, and tech like HUDs, turrets, and drones. Effective against vehicles to narrow crew awareness. Lasts for 2 turns.

title: Burnout
description: Connects to all devices on a network and overclocks the CPU of the to burn and disable them. Takes one turn to overclock, but permanently disables that device if successful. When used against vehicles, it automatically leads to a shutdown of non-essential systems to protect itself, effectively kneecapping them until the reboot process can start.
rulesText: [-5 Traceability] Causes a one turn timer to start on all enemy electronics, if the enemies don't react within that turn and disable their equipment using a Bonus Action- their electronics burn and are permanently disabled. Vehicle electronics are disabled for the next turn and need to restart.

title: Mass Crash
description: Much like Mass Hack and Burnout, Mass Crash also penetrates into an enemy's network- but goes even deeper. Going as far as to intrude into the local power grid to disable everything in the local area. Lights, power, and all enemy electronics are severed and shut down. Useful for creating either perfect darkness to escape, or an opening to push while hostiles. are confused and dazed.
rulesText: [-5 traceability] [Disables] all enemy electronics within the world hex. Disables radio, cameras, and tech like HUDs, turrets, and drones. Effective against vehicles to narrow crew awareness. Disables all non-natural lighting. Lasts for 3 turns.
